E037-01.notes: Past tense of 'lead' (to guide) is 'led'; 'lead' is the classic homophone trap. 'leaded' is not a verb form here; 'had lead' uses wrong participle.

E037-02.notes: 'It' cleanly refers back to the 'single small bag'; the contents and one dress emphasize light packing and match the record. A, B, D are off-goal.

flags: minor: passage says she 'continued by train to Amiens' after England, glossing over the Channel crossing to France; acceptable simplification
E037-03.notes: 'off of' is redundant/nonstandard; 'stepped off the train' is concise and idiomatic. 'off to' and 'out off' are wrong.

E037-04.notes: 'A number of' takes a plural verb; 'were following' also keeps past tense consistent. A, C, D are all singular (and C/D shift tense).

E037-05.notes: Rest of paragraph is about Cosmopolitan's competing reporter and neither woman knowing where the other was; C introduces the race and Bly's initial ignorance of it, which is historically accurate. A, B, D do not set up the Bisland race.

E037-06.notes: Object of preposition 'between' requires objective case 'her'. 'herself' lacks antecedent in-clause; 'hers' is possessive.

E037-07.notes: Needs the conjunction 'where' introducing the noun clause; others are homophone/near-homophone traps.

E037-08.notes: Past perfect requires past participle 'beaten' after 'had'. 'beat' as participle is colloquial; 'beated' nonstandard; 'beating' ungrammatical.

E037-09.notes: 'thousands of people jammed the station' is the only option conveying a large crowd; B-D are vague.

E037-10.notes: Only A ties back to editors' luggage objection from paragraph 1. D is accurate (a later traveler beat her time within months) but doesn't address editors' doubts; B and C are off-goal.
